title.narrative: Power to You(th) Malawi

description.narrative: The Power to You(th) Consortium believes that change starts within the community. We believein the power of young people, especially adolescent girls and young women (AGYW), beingmeaningfully included in discussions and decisions. Gender norms can be changed, and notonly AGYW but also boys and men, and sexually and gender diverse groups, can be positivecontributors to that process of change. Together we can achieve change with regards to harmfulpractices, sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) as well as unintended pregnancies.
Incoming commitment with Sonke Gender Justice

Whether or not legal frameworks are in place to promote enforce implement and monitor equality and non-discrimination on the basis of sex

title.narrative: Societal actors support and promote youth rights and progressive social norms (Changing social norms)
Level of public support for family planning and prevention of harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: Social welfare offices, chiefs, councillors, police, teachers, health workers, parents and churches are societal actors mentioned, whotake action to change practices. Many societal actors contribute to awareness raising. When it comes to law enforcement, depending on the type of law violations, chiefs and social welfare offices intervene with support from NGOs/CBOs. Also, police sometimes arrest perpetrators. Citizen�s voice and action committees, chiefs/village headmen play the biggest role in enforcing the bylaws.
No target set. Qualitative measurement

The initiatives conducted ensured that there was an interaction with societal actors, ensuring that that they have the relevant information and they are aware of their role in the fight against unintended pregancies, harmful cultural pratices and SGBV. Chiefs have also been supportive through the chiefs forum by raising awareness in their communities, in line with PtY themes. Parents through the Parents Teachers Association and Mother groups have also been supportive, by following up on school dropouts, to enusre that they go back to school.Religious leaders are also supportive of youth-centered initiatives, by deliberately having youth groups in the churches. They have also taken a step further to ensure that they are checking the age of couples during marriage ceremonies.

title.narrative: Societal actors support and promote youth rights and progressive social norms (Changing social norms)
Level of public support for family planning and prevention of harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: Social welfare offices, chiefs, councillors, police, teachers, health workers, parents and churches are societal actors mentioned, whotake action to change practices. Many societal actors contribute to awareness raising. When it comes to law enforcement, depending on the type of law violations, chiefs and social welfare offices intervene with support from NGOs/CBOs. Also, police sometimes arrest perpetrators. Citizen�s voice and action committees, chiefs/village headmen play the biggest role in enforcing the bylaws.
No target set. Qualitative measurement

Youth advocates engaged traditional leaders on the negative�s effectives of harmful practices and SGBV, and this resulted in commitment to support efforts on the eradication of such practices. Chiefs in T/A Sale committed to develop and formulate community by-laws to guard against SGBV. Additionally, the advocates also engaged health workers at health centres within their communities on family planning commodities and supplies, in places where there is perpetual shortage of the commodities, especially condoms. The healthworkers committed to ensure availability of the Family Planning and other SRH services commodities and supplies and to conduct frequent mobile outreaches in order to bridge the gap on accessibility of the youth friendly health services.

title.narrative: CSOs amplify young peoples voices to claim protect and expand civic space
Description of effective use of accountability mechanisms by citizens or communities and CSOs towards SRHR of all people (SRHR I)

comment.narrative: Some key informants referred to different development committees in the traditional Authorities(TA) as a way to hold communities accountable to the laws, by-laws, and policies in place. Recently the TA in Tambala has conducted a stakeholder mapping, so the TA has an overview of which organizations and institutions are active in the area, to be able to inform the communities about the plans and to know if the implementation is happening. The committees seem to be active, but some people from the community indicated that they were not informed by them.

In 2021 we concentrated on capacity building of CSOs, Youth Networks and community members on accountability monitoring processes and mechanisms. It is expected that in 2022, the communities, CSOs will start using the accountability mechanisms to monitor SRHR services for all people.

title.narrative: CSOs amplify young peoples voices to claim protect and expand civic space
Description of effective use of accountability mechanisms by citizens or communities and CSOs towards SRHR of all people (SRHR I)

comment.narrative: Some key informants referred to different development committees in the traditional Authorities(TA) as a way to hold communities accountable to the laws, by-laws, and policies in place. Recently the TA in Tambala has conducted a stakeholder mapping, so the TA has an overview of which organizations and institutions are active in the area, to be able to inform the communities about the plans and to know if the implementation is happening. The committees seem to be active, but some people from the community indicated that they were not informed by them.
No target set. Qualitative measurement

Youth networks have been actively involved in the use of community scorecards, as a tool for promoting accountability and improving the quality of public services, by giving community members a voice in the evaluation process and empowering them to take action to address areas where services are performing poorly. The youth networks at T/A Kasumbu expressed that the used the community scorecard process in the procurement of various items at the school, checking whether procurement processes have been followed and if the items are of good quality. The youth networks have also used the community scorecard process at the health facilities to assess service delivery at the community health facilities.The youth have also used the tool to monitor the utilization of funds in the construction of a school shelter at Nainunje school in Machinga.

# of women led CSOs using a Gender and Social Inclusion lens during all phases of the programming cycle with specific attention to youth

comment.narrative: PtY Malawi continues to work with the CSOs reached in 2021 and 2022 (35). The total number of CSOs added in 2024 is 4 (Not youth led or women led). in total 39 CSOs were provided with refresher training on GTA and participated in the Male Engagement for GBV Prevention Symposium. Advancement in CSOs who have been using a gender and social inclusive lens was demonstrated at the Symposium, where previously trained CSOs shared their experiences on integrating GTA in their interventions after engagements with PtY Malawi.

comment.narrative: PtY Malawi continues to work with the structures reached in 2021 and 2022. The total for the structures added in 2023 is 9 (2 youth-led csos, 1 csos not youth-led or women-led, 1 community, 5 advocacy networks). The structures have been trained in lobbying, advocacy and research. Some have contributed to the mid-term evaluation by compiling stories that were part of the research and some have been involving in lobbying and advocacy at community level with chiefs, on the enforcement of community bylaws and ensuring that gender related laws are known amongst the communities.

title.narrative: Young people demand accountability and responsiveness on key issues
# of young people (male) using SRH services who participate in policy and decision-making bodies who perceive their participation as meaningful

description.narrative: disaggregated in age brackets and by gender identity for m or x

comment.narrative: Young people have been able to participate in decision making structures at community and district level. They have been able to lobby for community bylaws on prevention of harmful practices, report cases of SGBV and ensuring that such cases are settled, they have been able to participate in structures such as the school management committee, village development committee, community victim support unit and chief's forum. The total number reached is 274 (152 female and 122 male). The reason for overachievement is due to some unfunded events which increased reach beyond what we had planned.

comment.narrative: Young people have continued to meaningfully participate in decision making bodies and have applied the knowledge and skills attained after engagements with the PtY coalition, to hold duty- bearers accountable. The total reach is 109 (49 Males 60 Females) The reason for underachievement is because the targets for 2024 were submitted prior to clarification of whether it was cumulative or not. However, we have achieved our target for the 5 years.
